THE HOLE, re-derived myself rather than read: fixtures.ts:206 computes `live = connection !== "DISCONNECTED" && !requiresAffordanceRefresh`, and :209 gates on `live && nextAllowedCommands.length > 0`. Both blocking legs are unobservable because every fixture that should be blocked also carries an empty command list — DISCONNECTED is built with EMPTY_NEXT_ALLOWED_COMMANDS (:228) and HISTORICAL inherits `historical.nextAllowedCommands` from contracts' historicalRuntimeResult(), which is also empty (:234). The test cannot catch it either: scaffold.test.tsx:175-176 re-derives production's own expression and compares it to production's own output — a tautology that tracks any formula change. :181/:183 assert false against fixtures whose emptiness already forces false, so neither leg is ever isolated.

Commit a3af231 added EPIC RAIL 6: "Assert the reason code, not just the outcome... A property must be asserted against the production surface, not against a test helper that reimplements it. These defects are invisible to a green suite: verify a failure-path test by mutating the production surface and confirming the test goes red." The rejected assertions are exactly the reimplemented-property case that rail now forbids. Both QA agents proposed rail 6 jointly after finding three instances in one session.

SIZE CONSTRAINT, and it is tight. Same commit rewrote EPIC RAIL 5: the 250/400 cap is PER PRODUCTION FILE, explicitly NOT per task, and there was never a per-task net-LOC budget. PLAN FOR THE FIX (small, per the rejection): add two leg-isolation snapshots that each carry NON-EMPTY commands so only the named leg can block them — a DISCONNECTED-with-retained-affordances case and a refresh-required-while-CONNECTED case. Then verify with three mutations, not one: QA's `const live = true`, plus each leg neutralised independently, since `live = true` alone cannot prove the two legs are separately observable.

A HARNESS BUG I CAUGHT IN MYSELF, worth recording because it is the exact defect epic rail 6 was added for. My first mutation script wrote its backup to `/tmp`, which node on Windows resolves to `D:\tmp` — every write threw ENOENT, no mutation was ever applied, and all four runs printed a comfortable "25 passed". Had I read only the pass counts I would have reported the fix verified while testing nothing — "a sweep that silently produces zero cases passes while testing nothing", verbatim. The rewritten harness asserts the anchor string exists, asserts the mutated body actually differs from the original, and prints CAUGHT/SURVIVED per mutation rather than a bare count.

WHY THE CANONICAL FOUR CANNOT DO THIS JOB (so a future edit does not "simplify" the isolation set away): each canonical state is blocked by more than one leg at once — DISCONNECTED is blocked by transport AND emptiness, HISTORICAL by refresh AND emptiness — so no single leg is observable through them. They are exported as a separate `MUTATION_BLOCK_ISOLATION` const rather than appended to `affordances` deliberately: `affordances` is keyed one-per-transport-state by consumers (the test asserts that key list), and two of the three isolation cases are CONNECTED, so appending them would collide on that key and change the shape five downstream surface tasks read.
